titleEn: Speak Softly, and the Ducks Come!

pages.text: "Ducks, come play with me!" Dingding shouted down from the bank. The ducks floated together in a circle. Dingding wanted to see them up close.
"Come this way!" Dingding cupped both hands around their mouth and shouted louder. Startled, the ducks scattered in every direction. Only splashes remained.
Dingding's voice echoed over the empty paddy. Instead of coming closer, every duck had disappeared. Dingding crouched on the bank.
Mr. Ming, who kept ducks in the lowest paddy, came up. "Ducks hide under the water plants when they hear loud sounds." "Because of my voice?" Dingding covered their mouth with both hands.

Mr. Ming took Dingding down to the water's edge, and they sat together. "We're here, little ones. Speak Softly, and the Ducks Come!" he whispered. One by one, the hidden ducks lifted their heads above the water.
Dingding tried whispering like him. "I'm here, little ones." One duck swam toward Dingding. Dingding held their breath and waited quietly.
The ducks gathered one after another at Dingding's feet. Paddy water tickled their bare toes. Dingding whispered very softly, "Speak Softly, and the Ducks Come!"

At the work-break meal, Dingding climbed to the high bank and stood beside Mom, who worked several paddies on her own. Dingding sniffed the meal's smell. Below, the ducks looked tiny as beans. "Can you hear me down there?" From this far away, the ducks were not startled at all.

Dingding knew how loud to speak now. "One, whisper beside the ducks! Two, speak loudly from high above! Three, lower my voice if they scatter!" The next day, Dingding stepped gently by the lower paddy. "It's me, little ones," they whispered.
Mr. Ming lifted Dingding into a hug. Speak softly when close, and loudly when far away. Dingding whispered into his ear, "Speak Softly, and the Ducks Come!"
